comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C20-C26 regarding osteoblast-specific conditional knockout mice. Both evaluations find the evidence strongly supported, with peer reviewers explicitly praising this finding as 'of high interest' and OpenEval noting the strong genetic evidence for cell-autonomous function in osteoblasts.

Perfect alignment on claims C27-C32 regarding Malat1-β-catenin interaction mechanism. Both evaluations strongly support the findings, with peer reviewers calling it 'interesting and novel' and the editor emphasizing its value beyond the bone field. OpenEval notes the complementary approaches (ChIRP, RIP, luciferase) while acknowledging some mechanistic details remain to be elucidated.

Perfect alignment on claims C33-C37 regarding non-autonomous function in osteoclasts. Both evaluations support the findings, though peer reviewers initially questioned the lack of phenotype in LysM-Cre deletion given prior reports, but ultimately accepted the evidence after revisions. OpenEval emphasizes the definitive contrast between global and osteoclast-specific knockouts.

Perfect alignment on claims C38-C48 regarding OPG-mediated crosstalk mechanism. Both evaluations strongly support the comprehensive experimental design including co-culture experiments, OPG expression analysis, and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers found the mechanism 'interesting and novel' while OpenEval praised the multiple lines of evidence.

Perfect alignment on claims C49-C58 regarding chondrocyte contribution to OPG regulation. Both evaluations support the findings after initial peer reviewer concerns about the role in chondrocytes were addressed. OpenEval emphasizes the novel cellular source identified by scRNAseq and extension of mechanism beyond osteoblasts.

Perfect alignment on claims C59-C60 regarding fracture healing model. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers initially requesting quantitative data enhancements that were subsequently addressed. OpenEval notes this extends findings from homeostatic to pathological bone repair conditions.

Strong alignment on bone phenotype claims C8-C19 (peer R1 excludes C7). Both evaluations find the comprehensive characterization well-supported. Peer reviewers praised the careful analysis with in vivo and in vitro systems, while OpenEval emphasizes the multiple complementary approaches demonstrating uncoupled bone remodeling.

Partial overlap on claims C7 and C10 regarding cortical bone observations. Peer R8 specifically addresses lack of cortical bone phenotype (C7, C10, C21) as supporting data distinguishing trabecular from cortical effects. OpenEval R1 includes these within broader bone phenotype characterization (C7-C19). Both find evidence supported.

OpenEval R8 evaluates background claims C1-C6 about Malat1 characteristics and prior work as well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval R9 evaluates general background claims C61-C67 about lncRNAs as well-established facts supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval R10 evaluates background claims C68-C74 about β-catenin signaling, OPG, and Jagged1 as well-supported by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval R11 evaluates background claims C75-C77 about bone remodeling and cellular crosstalk as established background supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval R12 evaluates abstract summary claims C78-C82 as accurately reflecting major experimental findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary statements, though peer reviewers' overall acceptance implies agreement.
